system_name: EU AI Act System Inventory & Vendor AI Classifier
system_purpose: A public web tool that processes unstructured AI system descriptions through a large language model to generate structured EU AI Act compliance classifications and obligation lists.
gpai_note: Uses Anthropic Claude (general-purpose large language model) hosted in the US, as supplied.
rationale: The system is a text processing and classification tool that takes unstructured input and generates informational output with no decision-making authority over natural persons or regulated entities. It does not perform recruitment, credit, insurance, biometric or other Annex III uses; it produces advisory text about legal classification, not binding determinations. The outputs are explicitly marked as machine-generated and informational. No Article 50 transparency duty is triggered because the system does not interact directly with natural persons in a way that materially affects them, does not generate synthetic media, and does not perform emotion recognition or biometric categorisation. It does use a general-purpose model, but that is orthogonal to the tier. The regulatory status of the tool itself under the Act is distinct from the fact that it offers guidance on the Act to others. Minimal risk is the default for a tool that produces informational output without authority to bind, harm, or influence decisions about individuals.
gaps: Who is the provider for compliance purposes—the individual operator, or the operator plus Anthropic as a value-chain partner? If the individual operates it commercially or under contract, they are the provider; if free and personal, it may fall outside the scope entirely.
Is the tool offered commercially in any context, or only made available free to the public? That may bear on Article 2 applicability and on the provider's role.
obligations: Art. 4 — take measures to support the development of AI literacy among staff and others operating or using the system on our behalf, proportionate to their technical knowledge, experience, education and training and to the context of use. The Article does not require any specific level of AI literacy to be guaranteed for any individual. Binds providers and deployers. In force since 2 February 2025.
No mandatory obligations under the AI Act at this tier, beyond any AI literacy duty listed above.
Art. 95 — voluntary codes of conduct may be applied.
Record the system in the inventory anyway: tiering is a point-in-time judgement and a change of use can change the tier.
Ch. V (Art. 53-55) — obligations fall on the provider of the general-purpose model, not on us as a downstream user. In force since 2 August 2025.
If we fine-tune a general-purpose model or place it on the market under our own name, we may become its provider and inherit those obligations — confirm before any fine-tuning project starts.
input_description: EU AI Act System Inventory & Vendor AI Classifier. A web tool built and operated by an individual in Luxembourg. A user pastes an unstructured description of an AI vendor or system; the tool sends it to a large language model (Anthropic Claude, hosted in the US) and returns a structured inventory row: whether the Act applies, the user's role, the risk tier, applicable obligations, legal basis, and questions still to ask the vendor. It classifies systems, not people; it makes no decisions about natural persons. Outputs are informational and marked as machine-generated. Made available to the public free of charge.
